samples.summary: The nesting-cap predicate is implemented twice (backend + frontend) instead of once in the shared `@wafflebase/docs` package that already owns the constant
samples.evidence: `hasDocsTableAtNestingCap` / `documentHasTableAtNestingCap` (packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:231-256) and `hasTableAtNestingCap` (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts, added in this diff) are the same walk over the same `Document`/`Block` model, with the same `depth >= MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH` rule, used to make the same refusal decision on the two producers of the same Yorkie tree. `MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH` itself was correctly put in `packages/docs/src/model/table-nesting.ts` and exported from both `src/index.ts` and `src/node.ts`, so the shared home exists and both sides already import from it; the backend also already imports `docsTreeToDocument` from `@wafflebase/docs` for exactly this reason (docs/design/README.md:159 records that sharing the docs converter with the backend was a deliberate decision after duplicated reader logic produced 'plausible-but-wrong content' silently). A third near-copy of the same accounting lives in `packages/docs/src/view/clipboard.ts` (`capTableNesting`) and a fourth in `Doc.tableNestingDepth`. If the two predicates drift, the backend accepts a body the editor refuses to write (or vice versa) — two answers to one invariant, which is precisely the failure mode the invariant exists to prevent.
searchedFor: docs/design/README.md revision-history entry on sharing docsTreeToDocument

samples.summary: Scope far beyond the originating issue: a whole nesting-cap subsystem (plus presence clamping, cycle guards, a merge-expansion budget) rides along with a two-item selection bug fix, reversing a documented design Goal
samples.evidence: The originating work item (docs/tasks/active/20260914-table-drag-merge-selection-todo.md, issue #1049) plans exactly: (1) resolve the table through `resolveNestedTableLayout()` in `selection.ts`, (2) make shift+click build an expanded `tableCellRange` in `text-editor.ts`, (3) tests — and its 'Out of scope' section names nothing else. This diff additionally introduces `MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH` enforcement across the docs package, the frontend store, the backend `docs-tree`/`DocumentCopyService`/`PUT /content` controller, the DOCX importer, both paste writers and the revision-preview snapshot adapter; a new `MAX_MERGE_EXPANSION_CELLS` approximation budget on the render path; peer-presence cell-rectangle clamping; and cycle guards on five `blockParentMap` walks. It also reverses a stated Goal of the canonical design doc — 'Recursive nesting with no hard depth limit' (docs/design/docs/tables/docs-nested-tables.md:19, rewritten here) — and commits the product to new user-visible refusals (a document copy refused with a 400, `writeFullDocument`/`writeDocsRoot` throwing, incremental edits silently declined). Each of those may be defensible on its own, but they are separate design decisions bundled into a selection-painting bug fix, so they land without their own issue, review, or rollback boundary.

samples.summary: Incremental writers silently drop a user's edit with only a `console.warn`; no product-level feedback path is specified
samples.evidence: `warnDeclinedTruncatedRowsWrite` makes `updateBlock`, `updateTableCell`, `setHeader`, `setFooter`, `insertTableRow` and `insertTableColumn` return without writing, leaving the cache untouched and reporting only to the browser console. The design doc section added here (docs/design/docs/tables/docs-nested-tables.md:326-333) argues throwing would abandon a command mid-way, which is reasonable, but the chosen alternative is an edit that simply does not happen with no signal a user can see — a behaviour the rest of the editor does not have. The doc records the decision but not how a user learns of it; at minimum the affected document becomes silently partially-uneditable.

samples.summary: `PUT /content` rejects one level more than the writer refuses: any *block* at depth 32 is 400'd, including ordinary paragraphs inside the deepest table the editor is allowed to create
samples.evidence: `assertValidBlock` now throws when `depth >= MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH`, where `depth` counts table-cell descents. The writer invariant is different: `buildBlockNode`/`writeDocsRoot` permit a table block at depths 0…31, and such a table's cell blocks sit at depth 32. So a document the editor can legitimately hold and `writeDocsRoot` accepts (deepest table at 31, paragraphs at 32) is rejected by the REST endpoint — an export/re-import round trip of that document 400s. The new design-doc text claims only that '`PUT /content` rejects such a body with a 400' for 'a table nested at or past the cap' (docs/design/docs/tables/docs-nested-tables.md:311), which is not what the check does. Practically unreachable content, hence minor, but the two enforcement points state different invariants.

samples.summary: The render-path behaviour changes (merge-expansion budget, presence rectangle clamping, nested-aware table lookup — i.e. the actual #1049 fix) are recorded in no design doc; only the nesting ceiling was documented
samples.evidence: The doc update in this diff covers `MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH` alone. Not recorded anywhere: (a) `MAX_MERGE_EXPANSION_CELLS`, a new policy under which a peer's cell-rectangle selection may paint short by design — presence-carried `tableCellRange` is documented at docs/design/docs/docs-presence.md:97 and says nothing about being clamped or budget-truncated; (b) `normalizeCellRange`'s clamping of peer-written row/col indices; (c) the fix the issue was actually filed for — `normalizeRange` and `Selection.getSelectedText` now resolving nested tables via `resolveNestedTableLayout`, which changes what copy/cut produce for a nested-table cell rectangle, while docs/design/docs/tables/docs-table-copy-paste.md:58-59 still describes the flat `layout.blocks` lookup. Per CONTRIBUTING/docs-design discipline these belong folded into the canonical subsystem docs (docs-presence.md, docs-table-copy-paste.md), not left undocumented.

samples.summary: `capTableNesting`/`capTableCellsNesting` enforce a model-level invariant but live in the view layer
samples.evidence: Both helpers are pure `Block[]`/`TableCell[][]` transforms keyed on `MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH`, which lives in `packages/docs/src/model/table-nesting.ts` alongside the other producers of the same invariant (`Doc.tableNestingDepth`, `Doc.insertTableInCell`). Placing them in `view/clipboard.ts` means the invariant is now spread across model and view; no behavioural consequence, but it makes the fourth copy of the nesting walk harder to consolidate later.

verdict.reason: Verified present and in-lane. `hasDocsTableAtNestingCap` (packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:231-245) and `hasTableAtNestingCap` (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:454-465) are byte-for-byte equivalent recursive walks with the identical `depth >= MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH` rule, gating the same refusal on the two producers of the same Yorkie tree (backend writeDocsRoot docs-tree.ts:376 and DocumentCopyService document-copy.service.ts:446; frontend writeFullDocument yorkie-doc-store.ts:3526-3528 and the incremental writers at :1049/:1097/:1884/:3114). Crucially, the backend's `DocsBlock`/`DocsDocument`/`DocsTableCell` are plain re-export aliases of `Block`/`Document`/`TableCell` from `@wafflebase/docs` (packages/backend/src/yorkie/yorkie.types.ts:15-25), so the two copies walk the same type and a single shared implementation is trivially available — the shared home already exists at packages/docs/src/model/table-nesting.ts:26, exported from src/index.ts:97 and src/node.ts:145, and the backend already imports from it (docs-tree.ts:35-41). The repo's own design record favors sharing exactly here: docs/design/README.md:159 documents that the docs tree converter was shared with the backend's readDocsRoot specifically because duplicated reader logic silently produced 'plausible-but-wrong content', and docs/design/docs/tables/docs-nested-tables.md:306-317 describes the 'no writer deletes rows it never read' refusal as one invariant that writeFullDocument and writeDocsRoot both carry. No refutation ground holds: the code is as described (not not-present); nothing makes either copy unreachable or keeps them in lockstep (no already-guarded); duplication/reuse is explicitly this lens's lane and the rubric grades divergence-prone duplicated logic as major (not out-of-scope). The only mitigation is the docs-tree.ts:3-28 header declaring the writer a deliberate mirror, but it justifies that by React/browser coupling, which does not apply to a pure Block[] predicate, and it explicitly anticipates extraction into @wafflebase/docs. Divergence would leave the backend accepting a body the editor refuses to write — two answers to the one invariant.
